basis:
Card carries no tradition/system field; the card frames an August 2016 question put to a tarot reader in Manhattan's Union Square Park who draws cards on the election, and asks both who will win and what will decide it, decided as Western tarot (Waite tradition per the snapshot). Input damage is material and is recorded here: the actual cards drawn are NOT supplied on the card, so no card-by-card Waite reading can be performed and none is fabricated; the call is built only from the card's stated facts — Clinton leads August polls, and her email controversy and the Clinton Foundation are already public controversies named in the setting, which in a question that explicitly asks 'what will decide it' function as the case's designated deciding-factor material. Confidence is reduced for the missing spread.
Reading on the given material: a front-runner carrying a live documents/secrecy scandal into the autumn is the classic Waite-arcana exposure pattern (Moon/High Priestess material surfacing against the favourite); the setting's singling out of emails and the Foundation, over every other campaign issue, marks them as the deciding weight in this reading.
[Section 8 quantity check] Lines: Clinton's email controversy live and escalating into the autumn (pressing on Clinton, strongest, directly on the 'what decides it' object); Clinton Foundation controversy (pressing, second front on trust); Clinton's August polling lead (supporting Clinton, but it is a snapshot line, not an autumn line). Main line: the documents-scandal line acting on the favourite. Band: an upset win for the challenger by a narrow, state-by-state band — not a landslide; the polling line caps the grade.
prediction_text: Main call: Donald Trump wins the 2016 US presidential election, defeating Hillary Clinton in the vote of 8 November 2016. What decides it: Clinton's email controversy — with the Clinton Foundation questions as the secondary front — eroding trust in the front-runner through the autumn campaign and breaking late-deciding voters to Trump in the decisive states; the election turns on the documents/secrecy scandal, not on policy or on the August polling lead, which does not hold. Spread limitation stated plainly: the drawn cards were not supplied with this case, so this call rests on the case's stated deciding-factor material and is held at reduced confidence.
